Identified as this saint because: The state seal of Tsar Petar I of Bulgaria, in Commons' category 'Peter I of Bulgaria' and carried as his portrait by the Bulgarian and the Russian Wikipedia articles on him. It is a crowned bust with the imperial insignia — the man, not a scene. This folder is that tsar: saint.gr prints «Άγιος Πέτρος Βασιλέας των Βουλγάρων», days.pravoslavie.ru «Петр Болгарский, царь» and the Ohrid Prologue „Свети Петар, цар бугарски“, Symeon's son, who reigned 927–967. The only other picture Commons holds in that category is the Manasses miniature of his death, which shows the funeral and not the man, and was passed over on the reasoning that already passed over the Peć burial fresco for Sava II. Commons describes it: Seal (state seal) of bulgarian tsar Petar I.
